basics.description: Deploys one CNQ Spark VM on Ubuntu 22.04 into an existing subnet in your subscription. Spark gets a private IP address only. Not for production use: no data protection, no support, provided as-is.

options.text: Spark is for scratch and non-production data only. It does not protect your data. If the VM fails or restarts you can lose everything on it.

basics.name: vmName
basics.label: VM name
basics.toolTip: Also becomes the Spark cluster name. 2 to 15 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen.

constraints.validationMessage: Use 2 to 15 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen.

basics.name: compute
basics.label: Size
basics.toolTip: Plus has twice the vCPUs of Standard. Azure bills the VM and the 1 TB disk at standard rates.

basics.name: vnet
basics.label: Virtual network
basics.toolTip: An existing virtual network in this subscription and in the region you chose above. Spark gets a private IP address only, so you need a network path to it (VPN, Bastion or a peered VM).

basics.name: noVnet
basics.visible: [and(not(empty(location())), contains(coalesce(basics('vnetsApi'), parse('{}')), 'value'), empty(basics('vnetsApi').nextLink), empty(filter(basics('vnetsApi').value, (v) => equals(toLower(v.location), toLower(location())))))]

options.text: No virtual network found in this subscription and region. Spark deploys into an existing virtual network. Create one in this region, with a subnet that has outbound internet access through a NAT gateway or a firewall, then open this form again. Or pick another region. You also need a way to reach the VM's private IP address, such as a VPN, Azure Bastion or a peered network.

basics.name: subnetId
basics.label: Subnet
basics.toolTip: A subnet of the virtual network above, with outbound internet access.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(basics('subnetsApi').value, (item) => and(not(equals(item.name, 'GatewaySubnet')), not(equals(item.name, 'AzureBastionSubnet')), not(equals(item.name, 'AzureFirewallSubnet')), not(equals(item.name, 'AzureFirewallManagementSubnet')), not(equals(item.name, 'RouteServerSubnet')))), (item) => parse(concat('{"label":"', item.name, '","value":"', item.id, '"}')))]

options.text: The subnet needs outbound internet access, through a NAT gateway or your firewall: HTTPS to GitHub, Qumulo and Azure Storage, and HTTP to Ubuntu's package archive. On first boot the VM downloads Spark, Docker and Qumulo Core.

toolTip.sshPublicKey: Generate a new key pair, use a key stored in Azure, or paste your own public key (RSA or ED25519). Never paste a private key.

options.text: Generating a key pair needs permission to create SSH keys in the resource group. Without it, the key dialog stays greyed out after you select Create: go back to Basics and pick Use existing public key instead. When it works, the portal downloads the private key once. Keep it: it's how you sign in to Spark as azureuser. The key stays in the resource group after you remove Spark.

basics.name: workEmail
basics.label: Email
basics.toolTip: Your email address, for example name@company.com.

basics.name: adminPassword
basics.toolTip: You sign in to Spark's web page and sudo spark with user admin and this password. It is stored on the VM in /etc/spark/admin-password (root only).

constraints.validationMessage: 12 to 64 characters, no spaces, double quotes or backslashes, with at least three of: lower case, upper case, a digit, a symbol.

options.text: When the VM first boots, it asks Qumulo for a Core download link. With that request it sends the email above and Microsoft's signed identity document for this VM, which names its VM ID and subscription ID. Qumulo keeps the email, the VM ID, a hash of the subscription ID, the region and the Core version for a year after the VM was last seen.

After the deploy, open https://<the VM's private IP>/ from a machine on this network, and sign in as admin with the password above. The certificate is self-signed: the browser warns once. To check it, compare its fingerprint with the one sudo spark web status prints.
